_comment: LAYER 2, for every substrate. The one file that is not about a cluster.
clusters/onprem/nodes.json describes the on-prem machines. clusters/gcp/cluster.json
describes the GCP project. This file describes neither: it holds the facts about how Argo CD
is installed, which ADR-0002 Layer 2 says must be the SAME everywhere, and ADR-0001's whole
premise says must not quietly stop being the same.
WHY IT EXISTS AT ALL, rather than each substrate carrying its own copy. The argocd role is
now run against three substrates (ADR-0020). It needs a chart version. There were three
places that version could live:
in nodes.json, read by the GCP inventory       - GCP then depends on an on-prem file, and
the next reader has to work out why
in both nodes.json and cluster.json           - two numbers that MUST agree, with nothing
making them agree. They agree until the
day one of them is bumped.
here, read by both                            - one number, and no way to disagree
The second option is the one worth naming, because it is the one that looks fine. Two copies
of a version pin is not duplication that costs an edit; it is duplication that produces a
cluster running a different Argo CD from its sibling, discovered by a behaviour difference
that nobody connects to a version for an hour. This repository has the same shape already in
clusters/onprem/nodes.json: the Kubernetes version lives there BECAUSE the Packer image
pins it, and the preflight role asserts the two agree rather than trusting them to.
So: anything both substrates must do identically belongs here. Anything about machines,
addresses, projects or zones does not.
Two different numbers. chart_version pins the HELM CHART; the chart decides which Argo CD
it installs, and 10.11.0 carries Argo CD v3.5.5. Check both when moving the pin -
`helm search repo argo/argo-cd --versions` prints CHART VERSION and APP VERSION side by
side - and keep the app version's minor matching the argocd CLI in
scripts/install-tools.sh, because a CLI far ahead of its server fails in ways that read
like permissions problems.
The role does not trust the pin to imply the app version: it reads back what the chart
actually installed and asserts it equals app_version. A chart patch release can carry a
different Argo CD.
_values_comment: ONE VALUES FILE FOR EVERY SUBSTRATE, and this was a decision rather than an omission.
Two things in it look on-prem-specific and are not:
global.domain / configs.cm.url - argocd.platform.local. Cosmetic: it is what the UI
prints in generated links. On GKE the UI is still reached by `make argocd-ui`, a
port-forward to localhost, because ADR-0003 forbids leaving a load balancer running. The
day GKE gets a real hostname, this becomes a per-substrate value and that is the moment
to split the file - not before.
the resource requests - sized for a 4 GB control-plane node. The GKE nodes are e2-medium:
2 vCPU and 4 GB, the same size. That is a coincidence rather than a reason, but it means
splitting the file today would produce two identical files.
server.insecure: true - correct on both, for the same reason: the server sits behind a
loopback port-forward. It is wrong the moment either cluster is reachable from elsewhere.
A second values file is the obvious next thing someone reaches for when a substrate needs
one different line. The cheaper answer is a per-substrate overlay passed as a second
--values, which keeps the shared file shared. Nothing needs it yet.
